title: Amulek Begins to Teach
summary: After speaking to the people, Alma sits on the ground. Amulek rises and begins teaching them about what they had been taught concerning Christ before their dissension.

explicit_facts.text: Alma sits on the ground after speaking to the people.
Amulek rises and begins to teach them.
Amulek says they had been taught about the coming of Christ, whom he calls the Son of God, before their dissension.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The audience is close enough to hear Amulek speak.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and audience members’ appearances are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: My brethren, I think that it is impossible that ye should be ignorant of the things which have been spoken concerning the coming of Christ, who is taught by us to be the Son of God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Amulek

narration.text: he sat down upon the ground, and Amulek arose and began to teach them, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma is present and seated as Amulek begins teaching.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ or his coming.

title: Faith in the Word
summary: Amulek recalls Alma's exhortation to faith and patience and addresses the people's question about Christ.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek recounts that the people asked Alma what they should do because of their afflictions, and that Alma exhorted them to faith and patience.
Amulek recalls the teaching to plant the word in their hearts and try its goodness.
Amulek says their great question is whether the word is in the Son of God or whether there shall be no Christ.
Amulek says Alma proved in many instances that the word is in Christ unto salvation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amulek continues speaking to the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's expressions and the way the word is visually represented are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And we have beheld that the great question which is in your minds is whether the word be in the Son of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The image of planting the word in hearts is figurative teaching, not a literal event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a literal seed or word planted in a heart.

title: Amulek Testifies of Christ

explicit_facts.text: Amulek recalls Alma's appeals to the words of Zenos, Zenock, and Moses.
Amulek testifies that Christ shall come among the children of men, take upon him the transgressions of his people, and atone for the sins of the world.

unspecified_visual_details: The cited figures and Christ's future coming are not described as present.

title: The Need for an Atonement
summary: Amulek teaches that all mankind would perish without an atonement and that the final sacrifice is infinite and eternal.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek teaches that an atonement is necessary under God's plan because otherwise mankind must perish.
He says the great and last sacrifice will not be a human, animal, or bird sacrifice, but an infinite and eternal sacrifice.

title: Justice and the Law
summary: Amulek uses the law concerning murder to explain that nothing short of an infinite atonement can suffice for the world's sins.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek says no person can sacrifice their own blood to atone for another's sins, and asks whether the law would take the life of a murderer's brother; he answers no.
He says the law requires the life of the murderer and that nothing short of an infinite atonement suffices for the sins of the world.

title: The Meaning of the Law
summary: Amulek explains that the law of Moses will be fulfilled and points to the Son of God as the great and last sacrifice.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek teaches that the great and last sacrifice brings a stop to the shedding of blood and fulfills the law of Moses in every jot and tittle.
He says the whole meaning of the law points to the great and last sacrifice, which will be the Son of God, infinite and eternal.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amulek continues teaching to the people.

title: Prayer in Daily Life
summary: Amulek teaches that they should pray over their flocks and households and against their enemies and the devil.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek tells them to cry unto God in their fields over their flocks.
He tells them to pray in their houses over their households morning, midday, and evening.
He urges prayer against the power of their enemies and against the devil, whom he calls an enemy to righteousness.

title: Prayer and Charity
summary: Amulek warns that prayer is vain if they turn away the needy, neglect the sick and afflicted, or fail to share their substance; he compares the uncharitable to discarded dross.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek says that turning away the needy and naked, failing to visit the sick and afflicted, and withholding substance makes prayer vain.
He compares those who do not remember charity to dross cast out by refiners and trodden underfoot.

The speaker says that those who postpone repentance until death become subject to the spirit of the devil, the Spirit of the Lord withdraws from them, and this is the final state of the wicked.
